narratives_meta.denominator: unbridged accounts (bridged fediverse accounts are in with_bridged)
narratives_meta.without_automated_definition: posts by accounts with p_automated >= 0.5, every like, repost and quote of those posts, and every like, repost and quote those accounts gave are removed; volume = posts + likes, reposts and quotes

meta.selection: every likely automated account (p_automated >= 0.5) with engagement, up to half the cap by degree; then the real accounts that engaged most with posts by accounts at p_automated >= 0.7; then the most engaged public accounts; then a seeded random sample of the 3,000 most engaged other accounts (kept only if linked). Edges among chosen accounts: engagement with likely automated accounts first, then earliest first.
meta.time_note: edge time is the like, repost or quote time; reposts carry no timestamp, so they use the engaged post's time (time_approx true). Nodes and edges are sorted by time; replay[h] gives how many of each are visible by the end of hour h (cumulative). Engagement after the story window stays in the arrays beyond the last replay hour.

sources.data: Bluesky AppView public API (api.bsky.app), no login; news: wire-service and public-broadcaster RSS and Google News RSS
sources.privacy: public accounts by handle; everyone else as a salted hash with no handle, post link or text

findings: Bluesky had 46,656 posts about the story from 20,495 accounts between Nov 5 and 13; 4.5% of posts (3.1% to 6.2%) came from likely automated accounts (score 0.5 or higher).

Among narratives with 30+ posts, "Board, resignation and succession" has the highest point estimate of likely automated posts at 7.7% (5.1% to 11%); its interval overlaps the story's 4.5% baseline (3.1% to 6.2%), so we call it suggestive, not a clear difference. "Jokes and memes" is the lowest at 0.4% and clearly below the baseline. The order of the point estimates holds at every score cutoff from 0.3 to 0.9. Removing likely automated accounts and their engagement leaves the narrative ranking unchanged.
On the Washington Post's 'online bots' claim: "Defending Huang" posts are 4.8% likely automated (2.0% to 8.7%), not clearly different from the story's 4.5% baseline.

630 real accounts amplified likely automated posts. Compared with similar accounts that saw the same story (616 matched on narrative, time window, reach, activity and followers), no archetype was clearly more likely to amplify them; "Often quote-posting, rarely reposting" accounts were less likely (0.46x, 0.26 to 0.66).

54% of wire-service and public-broadcaster headlines about the spy claim hedge ("alleged", "suspected", "claims"). On Bluesky, posts that share a link mostly keep the headline's wording (50% hedge), but posts written in people's own words drop it: 29% hedge. The caution survives the share button and disappears in the retelling.
